advice: Whiteflies transmit Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV). Install yellow sticky cards at canopy height and spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or acetamiprid early in the morning.

Blossom end rot is caused by localized calcium deficiency induced by erratic watering during rapid fruit swelling. Maintain uniform soil moisture using drip irrigation and apply foliar calcium chloride.
Deploy pheromone traps at 20 traps per hectare. Apply cartap hydrochloride or chlorantraniliprole granules into standing water during peak moth flights.

Blast disease spreads rapidly under high humidity (>90%) and overcast skies. Spray tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.6 g/liter or azoxystrobin. Temporarily drain standing water from paddies and withhold nitrogen top-dressing.
Apply propiconazole or tebuconazole 25 EC at 0.1% upon observing yellow or brown rust pustules. High humidity and mild temperatures accelerate spore germination on flag leaves.
Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) larvae bore into central leaf whorls. Apply emamectin benzoate 5 SG at 0.4 g/liter or spinetoram 11.7 SC directly into the whorl in early morning or evening.

Late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans thrives in cool, foggy, continuous drizzle. Apply systemic metalaxyl + mancozeb (2 g/liter) or cymoxanil upon first warning. Ridge soil high over tubers to prevent zoospores washing down.
For Mango, maintain balanced fertilization, ensure good drainage, and scout regularly for pest activity.

Murda complex is caused by thrips and mites. Upward leaf curling indicates thrips whereas downward boat-shaped curling signifies yellow mites. Spray spinosad 45 SC (0.3 ml/L) for thrips or propargite 57 EC (2 ml/L) for mites.
Monitor American bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera) using pheromone traps. Rotate spinosad 45 SC (0.3 ml/L), indoxacarb 14.5 SC (1 ml/L), and chlorantraniliprole to prevent insecticide resistance.
